# Independent audit: global supporting cuts and exact contact costs

**PASS in full**, with the minor cutting-hyperplane wording precision
recorded below. I read all four sections of
`candidate 6748c967393345b9`.
The projective seed theorem and the established convex-boundary radial
area formula are the stated mathematical dependencies. This construction
does not assert a universal payment inequality.

## Supporting slope selection

The finite Farkas certificate has the right sign: infeasibility of
`A.(z-p)>=h_z-h_p` would give nonnegative coefficients with zero base
moment and strictly positive support surplus. Normalizing their sum
contradicts the ACTUAL anchored Minkowski inclusion. Thus the majorant
is available at every source and normal, without assuming that the
source base is exposed or interior to the base hull.

The minimum-norm feasible slope is continuous. The KKT cone of active
row vectors has a linearly independent conic representation after
eliminating dependent positive coefficients. This yields one of finitely
many linear formulas in the support right-hand sides. On a convergent
subsequence with the same row set, feasibility, active equalities and
nonnegative multipliers persist, proving that the limit is the unique
minimum-norm slope at the limiting data. Empty active set gives zero.
The argument handles deficient row rank, unbounded feasible slope sets,
and support ties. Compactness of the normal sphere then gives the needed
uniform boundedness. No continuous-selection assertion is left unproved.

## Exact actual-body realization

For each fixed normal, the ambient cut is a convex inequality in BOTH
base and continuous coordinates: its nonlinear term is a positive
multiple of a globally finite convex function of an affine argument.
At epsilon zero it is a valid supporting inequality of the original
fiber hull. Intersection with all these cuts is therefore an actual
nested convex set. The fiber description (4) is an equality, not a
support-function approximation.

The inner homothet proof is uniform over the finite fibers and compact
normal/source parameter sets. Its points remain in the original fiber,
so the uniform bound on the nonlinear terms is indeed available there.
Every integer base remains occupied. Convexity and containment then
force the projection to stay exactly `conv(P)`, and completeness supplies
the asserted integer-base set. The rational orthogonal thickening for
deficient affine rank preserves those fibers; its scope correctly avoids
claiming containment in an initially supplied full ambient body.

With ONE source the own fiber is exactly its projective gauge erosion.
With several sources it may be eroded further. The statement makes this
distinction explicitly. Continuous base-denominator shifts are genuinely
free construction parameters; no denominator positivity away from the
source is needed because the tangent continuation is globally finite,
positive and convex.

## Contact-indicator first variation

At an old boundary point `x`, the unperturbed slack of cut `(i,u)` is

    h_z(u)-u.x+Delta_(i,z)(u)>=0.

It vanishes if and only if `u` supports that boundary point AND the
source cut has zero inter-fiber support gap. At a regular boundary point
the supporting unit normal is unique. This proves why the exact speed
in (5) is a maximum over zero-gap sources at that one normal, with zero
included if no source is active. Strictly slack normals cannot create an
unrecorded first-order cost by approaching the active normal: compactness
and continuity would force their limiting gap to be zero.

For the radial upper bound, an active perturbed constraint gives

    t_e u.(x-o_z)
       =epsilon Phi_(i,z)(u,x_t)
          -[h_z(u)-u.x+Delta_(i,z)(u)].

The bracket is nonnegative. Uniform `t_e=O(epsilon)` forces any limiting
active constraint to have zero old slack. Its denominator consequently
tends to the positive radial support distance, at least the chosen
inradius. Discarding the bracket gives exactly the required upper
bound. The lower bound comes from inserting every old active constraint.
If no old source constraint is active, the resulting limit is zero.

Thus the limit holds pointwise at regular boundary points even though
the final normal-dependent speed can be discontinuous across the closed
contact set. The uniform inner homothet provides domination, and the
radial cone Jacobian cancels the support denominator. The almost-everywhere
regularity of convex boundaries suffices; no normal-map continuity or
polyhedral approximation is used. The two-point `d=1` case is covered.

For a proper cap it is its CUTTING HYPERPLANE whose intersection with
the original body boundary is surface-null. The source initially wrote
‘a proper cut meets the old boundary’ in this sentence; I requested that
wording precision because the halfspace itself can contain positive
surface area. The proof and formula already use the correct cutting-
hyperplane fact. Inside supporting whole traces and outside supporting
empty traces have the claimed exact losses by nestedness, as do closed
pure-integer boundary fibers. Finite-menu uniform little-o control is
valid.

## Credit and retained scope

The own normal gap is identically zero, so the actual contact maximum
dominates each assigned projective seed at its own fiber. Containing
caps contain their parallel through-source cap, yielding the claimed
`Gamma_d` payment against the PRESCRIBED seed cost. Incoming erosion is
not silently charged to that same guaranteed coefficient. At shared
contacts, actual first costs and cap losses both use the maximum; no
sum of fictitiously disjoint removed masses occurs.

The fixed-cover signed row test, with original total mass and persistent
slack rows, is sufficient for actual global descent. Its positivity is
not claimed automatic. The source correctly identifies feasible support
slopes, base-denominator shifts and circuit selection as remaining
choices. It neither supplies a parity bound on cost nor suppresses any
same-cap input credit.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
